questions.stem: Which of the following lists the metals in order of decreasing reactivity?
questions.explanation: Reactivity falls in the order potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium, zinc, iron, lead, hydrogen, copper, silver, gold. Potassium loses its single outer electron most readily, while copper holds its electrons tightly and is found near the bottom.

distractorRationale.b: This is the correct series but written in increasing order of reactivity, not decreasing
distractorRationale.c: Magnesium is placed above potassium and copper above zinc, both the wrong way round
distractorRationale.d: Potassium, the most reactive of the four, is placed third

questions.stem: Which metal will NOT liberate hydrogen gas when added to dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Only metals placed above hydrogen in the activity series can displace hydrogen from a dilute acid. Copper lies below hydrogen, so it cannot give up its electrons to hydrogen ions and no reaction occurs with dilute hydrochloric acid.

distractorRationale.a: Magnesium is well above hydrogen and reacts rapidly, giving MgCl2 and H2
distractorRationale.b: Zinc is above hydrogen and gives a steady stream of hydrogen, the standard laboratory preparation
distractorRationale.c: Iron is above hydrogen and reacts slowly to give FeCl2 and H2

questions.stem: A strip of zinc is left standing in blue copper(II) sulphate solution. What is observed?

options.text: The blue colour fades and a reddish-brown deposit forms on the zinc
The solution turns a deeper blue and the zinc is unchanged
A white precipitate of zinc sulphate settles at the bottom
There is no visible change of any kind

questions.explanation: Zinc is above copper in the activity series, so it displaces copper: Zn(s) + CuSO4(aq) -> ZnSO4(aq) + Cu(s). The blue Cu2+ ions responsible for the colour are removed from solution as reddish-brown copper metal, which coats the zinc strip, and colourless zinc sulphate solution is left behind.

distractorRationale.b: Copper ions are being consumed, so the blue colour must fade rather than deepen
distractorRationale.c: Zinc sulphate is soluble in water, so it stays in solution rather than forming a precipitate
distractorRationale.d: No change would be correct only if the added metal were below copper, for example silver

questions.stem: Aluminium is extracted by the electrolysis of its molten oxide rather than by reduction with carbon because

options.text: aluminium oxide is too stable for carbon to reduce it
aluminium is a very poor conductor of electricity
aluminium oxide is insoluble in water
carbon is more expensive than electricity

questions.explanation: Aluminium is high in the activity series, so it holds oxygen very firmly and its oxide is extremely stable. Carbon is not a strong enough reducing agent to take that oxygen away, so electrical energy must be used instead. Only metals from zinc downwards form oxides that carbon can reduce.

distractorRationale.b: Aluminium is in fact an excellent conductor and is widely used in overhead power cables
distractorRationale.c: Insolubility in water is why cryolite is used as the solvent, but it is not the reason carbon fails
distractorRationale.d: Electrolysis is by far the more expensive route; it is used only because carbon reduction does not work

questions.stem: A piece of iron in contact with a block of zinc rusts more slowly than iron on its own.
questions.explanation: This is sacrificial protection. Zinc is above iron in the activity series, so zinc loses electrons in preference to the iron. The zinc corrodes away while the iron remains protected, which is why ships' hulls and underground pipes carry blocks of zinc or magnesium.

questions.stem: Which two substances must both be present for iron to rust?
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, so both oxygen and water are needed. This is shown by the classic three-test-tube experiment: iron in boiled water under oil, and iron in dry air over a drying agent, both stay bright, while iron exposed to air and water rusts.

distractorRationale.b: Dissolved carbon dioxide speeds rusting up by making the water acidic, but rusting happens without it
distractorRationale.c: Nitrogen is unreactive and plays no part in rusting
distractorRationale.d: Sunlight is not required; iron rusts just as readily in the dark

questions.stem: Which of the following reactions will take place as written? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A displacement reaction occurs only when the added metal is above the metal in the salt. Magnesium is above zinc, copper is above silver, and zinc is above iron, so those three proceed. Silver is below copper, so option c cannot happen.

distractorRationale.c: Silver lies below copper in the activity series, so it cannot displace copper from copper(II) sulphate; the equation is also wrongly written since silver sulphate is only sparingly soluble

questions.stem: In the blast furnace, iron(III) oxide is reduced according to Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2. Name the reducing agent in this reaction.
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide removes oxygen from the iron(III) oxide and is itself oxidised to carbon dioxide, so it is the reducing agent. In oxidation number terms carbon rises from +2 to +4 while iron falls from +3 to 0.
